beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Me and My Robots begins with three requests its narrator cannot answer comfortably.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Her mother wants to die, and her dead husband wants a thousand bodies.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A domestic robot has also lied about a wooden bird.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This science fiction novel brings autonomy into a family before expanding its institutions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its machines provide valuable care without making consent a solved problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its intimate disagreements reveal what people may need to refuse from good protection.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Kite can handle fragile paper and hold a failing ceiling in place.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its practical competence makes the household depend on more than a convenient appliance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The narrator must distinguish a request for safety from permission to detain someone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A paper envelope carries a decision that cannot be reduced to a risk estimate.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel lets ordinary objects concentrate disagreements about continuity and control.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That makes its philosophical questions intimate before they become public disputes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The journey reaches communities that organize dependence and departure through different rules.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their members cannot escape obligations simply by choosing a simpler way of life.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A workshop then places a handmade viola beside its technically superior copy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The comparison asks what people value when utility becomes abundant.
